Team — sending a concise readout for the week. Focused sections below: quick wins, immediate signals/risks that need leadership input, and concrete asks for the QBR pack. I attached a draft slide set and the telemetry appendix. Please skim the highlights and flag anything that should move to the QBR narrative.

Wins (this week)
- Redwood Dedicated: live pilot with Acme Cloud completed performance baseline; 35% better tail latency vs our standard route under their traffic pattern.
- Optimize: auto-batching suggestion engine rolled out to two internal customers; observed ~18% token cost reduction without noticeable latency regression.
- Console: new model-level cost breakdown released to internal alpha (Monica-led) — early feedback positive.

Signals / Risks
- Capacity friction in eu-west-2: some Dedicated customers saw scheduled job queues spike during nightly checkpoints. Short-term mitigation: bumped reserved slots for two clusters (temporary). Need a decision on capacity commit for Q1.
- QBR narrative: we should be explicit about cost-per-inference trends; current charts show improvement, but tooling-level explanations are still weak.
- Security/compliance: a SOC evidence request from Acme procurement landed (see external thread); they want KV cache policies documented for private deployments.

Asks (clear asks with owner & ETA)
- (Vivek) Decide whether to convert the bumped eu-west-2 capacity into a committed reserve for Q1. ETA: EOD Tue (Nov 16).
- (Markus) Approve the one-slide lift describing cost-per-inference drivers for QBR (slide 6). ETA: Mon (Nov 15).
- (Monica) Add a short note on alpha feedback summarizing adoption signals + two customer quotes to slide 3. ETA: Wed (Nov 17).
- (Laura) Help prioritize the SOC evidence pack items for Acme. They need KV cache docs and retention statements by Nov 20.

Notes: attached are Horizon_QBR_slides_v1.2.pdf (draft) and OKR-telemetry-brief.xlsx. I kept this intentionally short — call if you want to triage live.

Thanks,
Rachel
